neighbours.label: narrative about named figures of scripture or classic drama (Moses, Abraham, Macbeth, Othello)
fire: In the story, Noah built the ark and gathered the animals before the flood.
When Goliath mocked the army, young David stepped forward with his sling.
Jacob worked seven years so that he could marry Rachel.
In the final act, King Lear carries the body of Cordelia onto the stage.
Hamlet tells Horatio that there are more things in heaven and earth than he dreams of.
Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
Students should explain why Brutus joins the plot against Caesar.
Joseph forgave his brothers after they came to Egypt to buy grain.
quiet: In the story, the farmer built a barn and gathered the animals before the storm.
When the coach mocked the team, the young striker stepped forward to take the penalty.
My uncle worked seven years so that he could buy a small house.
In the final act, the orchestra plays the main theme once more.
The teacher tells the class that there is more to learn than they imagine.
The mayor challenged the council members at the meeting on Monday.
Students should explain why the company joins the new trade group.
The landlord forgave the tenants after they paid the missing rent.

notes: Probe: Moses/Macbeth/Abraham sentences 0.51-0.58, Othello 0.38, Peter 0.28, Patriarchs 0.14; modern manager/company analogues 0.01-0.03; 'God has blessed us' 0.01 (devotional language is the + pole). Peaks fall on later tokens (his, fathers, '.'), so a context rather than the name token.
